title: Wendell and the Promise
premise: Ten years ago, cellist Quentin Coldharbour walked off stage mid-concert and out of the life he shared with violinist Marguerite Voss, leaving her a promise he never explained. When a snowstorm traps him, Marguerite, and her fiancé—a rival conductor—in the island inn where they once summered together, three decades of silence thaw into confession. Quentin must finally speak the sentence he rehearsed for a decade: why he left and that he has loved her every day since. In the end, Marguerite chooses neither man as they were, but a future rewritten on her own terms—with Quentin, if he can stop hiding behind his cello.
about_author: Elodie Ravensworth is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent fifteen years cataloguing other people's love letters to music. She writes from a drafty cottage on the coast, where she keeps a broken metronome on her desk as a reminder that timing is everything.

chapters.title: The Ferry That Didn't Come
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Fleeing a humiliating comeback recital, Quentin takes the last ferry to Greywether Island, only to find Marguerite and her fiancé Aldous stranded at the same inn by an early snowstorm. Forced to share a dinner table, old wounds surface beneath polite conversation. The emotional beat is dread laced with longing—the past arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: What the Snow Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Quentin and Marguerite. Snowbound with no ferry for days, the trio uncovers a letter in the inn's attic revealing the island's disputed inheritance—and mirroring Quentin's own abandoned legacy of the Coldharbour estate. Marguerite confronts Quentin about the concert he fled. The beat is rising tension: secrets pressing against thin walls.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, climax. During a blackout, Aldous discovers Quentin's decade-old unsent letters and forces the confrontation everyone has avoided. Before the morning ferry arrives, Quentin finally speaks the rehearsed sentence—confessing why he left and that he never stopped loving her. The beat is raw catharsis; the truth costs him everything and frees him at once.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, resolution. With the ice breaking, Marguerite ends her engagement not for Quentin but for herself, claiming her inheritance of the inn and her own voice. She asks Quentin to stay—not as penance, but as choice. He unpacks the cello he swore was retired. The beat is quiet, earned belonging: love in the present tense at last.
